system.summary: Two-part code of 700 numbered cells: letters, syllables, common words and a few names, numbers in no order against the values.

prior_solution.where: Casgrain, Collection des manuscrits du maréchal de Lévis III (1890), prints all four letters in figures with the period clear text; the table itself had not been identified or transcribed.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.

solution.what: Transcribed Casgrain's four code I letters (figures and clear lines) against the page images.
Aligned the figures with Casgrain's clear text to get code I values (281 groups; not part of this folder).
Fetched the ten LAC images of ANOM COL C11E 10 (e001295267-76); sheet e001295272 is 775 px wide, cells 1-20 off the photograph.
Two blind passes over the 700 cells (A forward, B backward, separate agents, no code files); 609 of 680 legible cells agree; differences settled on 6x crops; table and test plan frozen (sha256).
Pre-registered comparison with our code I values: 188 of 273 exact against at most 3 for 200 shuffled tables; codes B and W: 0 agreements.
Decoded the four letters with the frozen table alone: 0.921-0.939 similarity to Casgrain's clear text, shuffled tables at most 0.352 (measure chosen after the plan).
Applied the table to Montcalm's 21 Nov 1758 letter to Bougainville (code B, 112 groups): 0 exact.

Searched New France Archives, C11A 103-104, the F3 inventory of 1899, NY Colonial Documents X and Casgrain for more code I text; found F3 15 f.194 (Montcalm to the minister, 1 Sep 1758, cipher with interlinear decipherment) and the cipher postscript of 12 Apr 1759, neither online.
Five Trémais groups (1759) looked up in the table: no sense; his letters use stacked groups, a different system.

Integration check of PR #583 (round 13). The four sha256 values of key/FREEZE.txt match the files. decode_letters.py re-run: all four similarities and shuffle figures identical (0.938, 0.921, 0.939, 0.935). An own decoder from the frozen table gives the same four decode files. Strict word count, table alone, a word of Casgrain's text counted only when every letter of it comes from cells marked clear: I1 82 of 122 (67.2%), I2 23 of 31 (74.2%), I3 169 of 233 (72.5%), I4 265 of 371 (71.4%); with doubtful cells also counted 79.5, 83.9, 82.0 and 82.7%. Table against the LAC image e001295272 (same sha256 as recorded), 80 cells of blocks 301-394 and 401-494 read at five times enlargement: 71 agree; 8 of the 9 differences are on cells the table marks doubtful (one, 474 t, is the contributor's own post-freeze correction), 1 on a clear cell (492). Outcome method changed from 'read after matching with key from external sources' to 'read from existing decipherment': the text is Casgrain's printed clear text.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1292 tokens, 273 types, fr-1750-nospace order 4: reading -2.13 per letter; random keys -3.164 (z 11.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.198 (mean -2.212, z 8.4); annealer on the real text -2.167. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.13; polyphony 0.0; 15 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.167

outcome.method_basis: The text of the four letters is the period decipherment as Casgrain printed it in 1890. The period deciphering table, transcribed blind from the archive image, was matched to those letters afterwards; the table alone does not give the text (integration check, 14 Nov 2026).

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: identification of sheet e001295272 as the Marine's 1758 table for Montcalm (code I), its transcription in two blind passes and the test against Casgrain's letters; no new reading. Not rechecked by a second agent.
The Marine ministry's clerks: the deciphering table (ANOM COL C11E 10 f.288) and the decipherments of the four letters.

texts.label: I1, Claude-Louis d'Espinchal, 26 August 1758
texts.summary: Massiac answers the news of the fall of Louisbourg (Île Royale): he is sending a corvette at once, and the King expects Montcalm to support Vaudreuil and Bigot and keep up the troops and inhabitants.
texts.note: The reading is the period decipherment as Casgrain printed it, complete for every paragraph. The decryption file is our decode with the frozen table alone, kept to show how far the table reproduces it (results/letters_test.json); it is not the reading.

reading_review.by: Andrew Beling's own AI agents (not a person, not an outside check)
reading_review.note: Casgrain's French read whole against our English; the table-only decode compared with it by script (92-94% similarity, no shuffled table above 35%). No new reading: the clerks and Casgrain read these letters first.

gaps.detail: Off the top edge of the LAC photograph; ANOM COL C11E 10 f.288 would settle them.
Short syllables at 775 px; a better image is needed. Seven are shown wrong by the letters (key/corrections_post_freeze.tsv).

outcome.notes: No new plaintext: the letters were read by the clerks and printed by Casgrain. The contribution is the identification and transcription of the period table and its blind test. No other text in this code was found online (NOTES.md).
